title: Windowed Node Rotation Automation (Sentinel) for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Liam Chen
description: Build a deterministic, windowed node-rotation service ("Sentinel") that automates draining, OS/container upgrades, and node replacement in Dedicated fleets while preserving throughput guarantees and autoscaling behavior. The automation must respect customer-configured maintenance windows, enforce safe capacity buffers, integrate with autoscaling policies, and provide clear audit trails and rollback hooks.
background: We have recurring operational toil around ad-hoc node drains and emergency upgrades that cause transient throughput stalls for Dedicated customers. Existing solutions are manual or reactive; they do not coordinate with the autoscaler or route-aware throttling. This ticket defines a new automation agent that runs scheduled, prioritized rotations with safety checks (prefix/KV cache warmup, slow-start traffic ramp, canary node upgrades) and offers visibility in Console.
decisions: 1) Use a controller-based approach running in the control plane so customer VPCs are not required to run agent software. 2) Rotation will be windowed: customers may specify weekly windows and blackout windows; default is 02:00-06:00 UTC. 3) Maintain a configurable 'buffer capacity' expressed as a percentile of baseline throughput (default 15%) to preserve throughput SLOs during rotations. 4) Integrate with existing autoscaler API: rotations should signal 'scale-lock' to prevent scaling down during critical phases.
tradeoffs:
- Proactive rotations reduce surprise failures but add scheduling complexity and potential extra cost for maintaining buffer capacity.
- Control-plane implementation avoids on-customer-host agents but increases cross-account orchestration surface and tracing complexity.
- Default buffer is conservative; smaller customers may prefer lower buffers to reduce cost (configurable).
acceptance_criteria: Customers can configure maintenance windows and blackout windows in Console and via API.
Sentinel performs a staged drain: cordon -> graceful drain respecting in-flight requests -> KV cache snapshot -> node replacement/upgrade -> warmup -> release traffic.
During a rotation, platform telemetry must show < 2% request error increase and token-level latency P95 within SLO for 95% of rotations in test runs.
Autoscaler respects 'scale-lock' during warmup/drain phases and resumes afterwards; no oscillation loops introduced.
Audit logs and Console timeline show start/end timestamps, decisions, and links to PR/upgrade artifacts for every rotation.
Rollback path: if warmup fails (throughput drop or error spike), Sentinel stops rollout and either retries or reverts to previous node image based on policy.
updates: 2026-02-20: Design review completed with infra, runtime, and console teams. Action: add 'buffer capacity' knob and a per-customer throttle multiplier.
2026-02-28: Prototype controller written; initial e2e in ephemeral region shows successful rotation without evicting KV caches. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5684
2026-03-03: Load tests (synthetic RL workloads) show increased request tail latencies when buffer < 10%. Decided default buffer 15%.
2026-03-05: Discovered autoscaler race where immediate scale-down after drain caused underprovisioning in canary phase. Added 'scale-lock' API and unit tests. Patch in PR 5697.
2026-03-09: UX mockups for Console maintenance settings reviewed by PM and Design. Need additional copy for 'estimated cost impact'.
2026-03-10: Blocker identified: RBAC for control-plane injector in Private deployments requires security sign-off. Opened ENG-24890 to track.
implementation_notes: Controller will reconcile per-fleet rotation objects and enforce a finite-state machine: SCHEDULED -> CORDON -> DRAIN -> UPGRADE -> WARMUP -> UNCORDON -> COMPLETED/FAILED.
Draining policy: attempt graceful termination with a 90s soft timeout, then escalate to force-terminate after configurable backoff.
KV cache warmup: after upgrade, warmup will replay recent prefixes from a per-fleet cache store; if warmup throughput < 80% baseline in 10 minutes, mark canary as failed.
Autoscaler integration: sentinel will call autoscaler API to request min-capacity bump and set 'scale-lock' via annotation until warmup completes.
testing_plan: Unit tests for FSM transitions and scale-lock interactions.
Chaos test: randomly fail upgrades mid-warmup and verify rollback behavior.
Staging e2e: run rotations across 5 simulated fleets with differing traffic profiles and verify throughput SLOs over 100 rotations.
Load validation: run real-client replay using production traces to validate latency, error rate, and token-cost impact.
Security review: run RBAC/privilege audit for control-plane orchestration in Private deployments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): Rollout to internal Redwood Dedicated fleets only. Monitor for 2 weeks.
Phase 1 (beta): Offer opt-in to select customers with small fleets and low throughput SLAs.
Phase 2 (general): Default enable for new fleets with conservative buffer; existing fleets opt-in after review.
Contingency: Immediate 'pause-all-rotations' flag in control plane for emergency aborts.
notes: Goal is to reduce manual maintenance hours and eliminate ad-hoc outages caused by uncoordinated drains. Keep open the possibility of an alternate lightweight agent if control-plane orchestration proves too restrictive for air-gapped Private installs.
